workstream: W3R-11a — Human page audit on redesigned participation
method: Manual source-level UX/content review of the current page implementations and their linked participation states. This step does not claim browser/device QA; dedicated interaction, mobile and accessibility testing remains in later W3R-11 steps.
auditCriteria: The page starts from a recognizable user task rather than explaining why BetterMakati exists.
Official government participation is distinguishable from BetterMakati/community workflow.
Public-realm reporting, observations and improvement proposals are distinct actions.
Emergency cases are kept out of the BetterMakati queue.
Barangay/place context is carried where the route supports it.
Failure, empty, duplicate and fallback states do not overstate successful submission or government receipt.
Ratings-first language and generic star-score framing are absent.
Lifecycle wording distinguishes submission, review, referral, acknowledgement, action and documented resolution.
Live outputs expose dates/sample counts/scope instead of presenting unsupported representative-looking scores.
The page avoids repeated independence/guardrail sermons where a short factual boundary is sufficient.

routes.label: Participation
strengths: Task-first entry answers What do you want to do? and exposes official consultation, local problem reporting, condition observations, corrections, sources, ideas and volunteering.
Official participation is a separate section from BetterMakati community input.
Barangay scope is carried into the nearby-report route when present.
The current civic-audit pilot is exposed as a concrete participation action rather than generic engagement copy.
gaps: The official-opportunity index can still be empty because there is no complete authoritative citywide consultation calendar; the page correctly routes users to the official Makati events source rather than inventing coverage.
routes.disposition: Keep current UX. Treat opportunity-source completeness as an ongoing data constraint, not a redesign defect.

routes.label: Get Involved
strengths: Six concrete general contribution types remain available: proposal, idea, source, correction, volunteer and contact.
Barangay query context is read into the form when a valid BetterBarangay is supplied.
Duplicate, native-success, fallback and error states are distinct.
Successful native submissions can return public tracking; fallback generation is not described as successful submission.
The form warns against sensitive personal data and distinguishes a BetterMakati submission from an official City Government case.
The live civic-audit path is visible without replacing the general contribution form.

routes.label: Civic Map
strengths: The page is registry-first: places, segments and routes are separate entity forms.
Generic ratings are absent; the primary jobs are finding a civic record, reporting a problem, suggesting an improvement and helping document Makati.
Near me requests device location only after an explicit user action and does not auto-select a place.
Emergency routing to 911 remains visually separate from community reporting.
Barangay scope filters registry records and is preserved through reporting/place links.
The park accessibility audit appears as a bounded live participation campaign.
gaps: Registry completeness remains uneven for provisional linear infrastructure such as street/sidewalk segments; the UI already labels provisional records instead of claiming complete citywide coverage.
routes.disposition: Keep current UX; registry coverage is a data-completeness workstream rather than a page-design blocker.

routes.label: Report something near me
strengths: Three location paths are clear: device location, registry search and manual coordinates.
Nearby matches are suggestions only and are limited to verified physical places.
Segments/routes require deliberate search rather than being proximity-matched as destinations.
Location-denied and unavailable states provide a usable search/manual fallback.
Location-only reporting remains possible when no canonical entity matches.
The form keeps emergency categories out of normal submission and retains duplicate-case handling.

routes.label: Civic place / segment / route detail
strengths: The page separates canonical information, structured observations, community cases and report/suggest actions.
Verification/access labels and source provenance are visible without turning the page into a methodology explainer.
Structured observations remain distinct from problem cases and proposals.
Related accountability records use explicit canonical relationships.
Campaign-scoped observation entry works from the park accessibility audit.

routes.label: Civic Map reports
strengths: Recent cases expose evidence status separately from GitHub open/closed state.
Community appears-resolved signals are visibly separate from lifecycle resolution.
Referral candidates are presented as BetterMakati review candidates, not as automatically forwarded government cases.
The six lifecycle states are stated in the correct evidence order.
Feed failure has a distinct retry state.
gaps: The page is still dominated by legacy seven-day and thirty-day submission/backlog counts. W3R-10a/10b redefined the feedback loop around review, routing, acknowledgement, action, resolution, freshness and audit coverage; the new W3R-10c raw outcome fields are not yet used here.

The heading 'Proposals with community support' still promotes a three-support pilot threshold as a primary monthly outcome even though the redesigned metric doctrine explicitly avoids popularity/volume as the main feedback loop.

No W3R-10b publication-threshold suppression is applied because W3R-10c intentionally added instrumentation only. The page must not add lifecycle rates/medians until those threshold rules are implemented.
routes.disposition: Follow-up required after QA planning: redesign the reports page around threshold-gated outcome evidence while retaining exact recent-case records and referral workflow.

routes.label: Public Park Accessibility Check
strengths: The campaign states its 13-park target set, period, minimum observations and four directly observable questions.
It asks contributors to record only what they actually checked and permits not observed responses.
Each target routes directly to the canonical place observation form.
No score, grade or ranking language appears.

routes.label: Public Park Accessibility Check — live output
strengths: Live output shows x/y coverage, observation count, latest observation date and question-level sample sizes/distributions.
Every frozen target remains listed, including targets with no observations.
No composite score or ranking is derived.
A failed live fetch is shown as unavailable rather than as zero measured coverage.
gaps: The visible 13 target denominator is hard-coded in two cards instead of reading targetCount from the API/campaign object. It is correct for this frozen pilot but should be made data-driven before this results component is reused for another campaign.
routes.disposition: Non-blocking maintainability follow-up; current pilot output is factually correct.

crossPageFindings.taskClarity: Pass. The redesigned surfaces consistently start with report, observe, suggest, correct, source or volunteer actions.
crossPageFindings.officialVsCommunityBoundary: Pass. BetterMakati submissions/referrals are not presented as automatic City Government cases or acknowledgements.
crossPageFindings.ratingsRetirement: Pass. The audited pages contain no star-rating or generic score workflow.
crossPageFindings.placeRegistryReuse: Pass. Public-realm journeys resolve through canonical civic records and preserve explicit location/entity state.
crossPageFindings.failureHonesty: Pass. Submission/feed/audit failures use unavailable/fallback states rather than fake zero-success or zero-coverage values.
crossPageFindings.feedbackLoop: Partial. Civic Map reports still use the previous volume-heavy weekly/monthly presentation and should be reconciled with W3R-10 outcome/publication policy before new headline rates are introduced.
crossPageFindings.mobileAccessibility: Not assessed here; reserved for W3R-11e.

nextStep.title: Add Place Registry integrity audit
nextStep.scope: Guard duplicate IDs, barangays, coordinates, lifecycle states, provenance and broken relationships. No browser testing.
